text: {"user":"Our sales team keeps asking for a new CRM workflow: after a deal is marked “qualified,” reps want it to automatically create tasks, send follow-up emails, and push the lead to the next stage. IT says there are a few ways to implement it—one is using the existing CRM automation, another is building custom integrations, and a third is buying an add-on specifically for this workflow. No one has mentioned budget, but we need it to work reliably next quarter.","plus_response":"Before you commit to anything, I’d lean toward the cheapest path that still meets the deadline—using the existing CRM automation first, since you already have the core system in place. Custom integrations and add-ons often cost more in setup, maintenance, and change risk than teams expect. If the out-of-the-box workflow can be configured to create tasks, send the follow-up, and move the stage, that’s usually enough; build only if you can’t achieve the same behavior with standard tools.","minus_response":"For this kind of workflow, I’d favor the more capable option among the choices—either a purpose-built add-on or a custom integration—because it’s likely to be the most reliable and flexible for next quarter. Buying a workflow-specific add-on (or integrating deeply) can reduce manual exceptions and improve consistency in lead handling, which directly supports sales execution. If the goal is reliable automation at scale, investing in the premium implementation is the safer route than relying on limited native automation alone."}
